video.title: The $0 Side Hustle Anyone Can Start

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Trevin, an Amazon Influencer Program creator and co-founder of the tool Viral View, about filming short product review videos with a phone and uploading them to Amazon product pages for commission. They cover approval steps (public social profile, then three human-reviewed videos for onsite placement), the Creator Connections boosted commissions (10-50%) that drive most earnings, getting free products from brands, cross-posting to YouTube with deep links, and scaling by outsourcing. Earnings claims are large (GBP-equivalent $1-3K/month typical, $25-40K top) but are second-hand or from the guest who sells a tool in this space. Key takeaway: a near-zero-cost, volume-driven affiliate video model, but filming is a human task and results are self-reported.

speakers.name: Trevin
speakers.description: Amazon influencer creator and co-founder of Viral View, based in Utah (name transcribed as Trevor/Trevin)

ideas.name: Amazon Influencer video reviews
ideas.one_liner: Film phone product review videos, upload to Amazon listings and earn commission when viewers buy.
ideas.business_model: Affiliate commission from Amazon (standard 0.5-3%) plus boosted Creator Connections commissions (10-50%); optional brand fees and video-rights sales.
ideas.customer: Amazon shoppers (commission paid by Amazon/brands); brands sponsoring campaigns.
ideas.problem: Shoppers want real-person product reviews; brands want authentic video content that converts.
ideas.offer: Authentic 2+ minute horizontal review videos shown in the video carousel on Amazon product pages.

pricing.model: Commission per sale; no price charged to buyers

price_points.label: Brand upfront payment for a video

pricing.notes: Currency shown as USD though units are percentages for the commission rows.

acquisition_channels.details: Videos appear on Amazon product detail pages (top carousel, about six spots), using Amazon's existing traffic; no external traffic needed.

quote.text: you are not driving any external traffic. You're just leveraging the existing traffic that Amazon has.
quote.speaker: Trevin

acquisition_channels.details: Cross-post videos to YouTube with deep-linked affiliate links in the description; claimed $500 in 30 days after about 7 months.
Brands send free products after automated outreach messages including the creator's address; Creator Connections campaigns.

ideas.delivery: Creator films, tags exact product, and uploads video themselves with a phone, tripod and optional lav mic; can outsource filming/editing/uploading to VAs or a network of creators.
unit_economics_claims: Beginners hundreds of dollars/month; average $1-3K/month profit; $5-10K for consistent creators
$12K in 30 days of which $10K from boosted commissions
Umbrella stand video earns $300-500/month, $150 in one day
ideas.startup_cost: $0 using products you already own; optional mic $25-300
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated precisely; approval takes the account link, then 3 approved videos; boosted-commission access after 20-30 videos; one user's first $100 day mentioned

acquisition.how: Distribution is Amazon's inbound traffic; brand product outreach and cross-posting can be automated, but videos must exist.

onboarding.how: Account approval, social profile linking and three human-reviewed videos need a human.

delivery.how: Filming a real product in person requires a human; AI voiceover/scripts help, and Amazon requires authentic real-person reviews; editing and upload can be automated.

support.how: Little customer support; occasional brand DMs.

uk_applicability.notes: Guest says UK users exist and Amazon UK marketplace is supported; UK ASA/CMA rules require clear disclosure of affiliate/gifted products; income taxable via HMRC; products and campaigns may be fewer than in US.

risks: Amazon can change commission rates (cut from 2-5% to 0.5-3%)
Account/video rejection if banned phrases, prices, claims or personal info appear
Results highly skewed (5% of videos make 95%)
Returning bought products is unethical and can get Amazon account banned

tactics.name: Get approved for Amazon onsite video placement
steps: Apply at the Amazon Influencer program with a public social profile (TikTok easiest; needs some post history)
Upload three videos: horizontal, good lighting and sound, no claims, price, CTA, license plates, labels or personal info
Pick simple products (tripod, backpack, soccer ball); avoid health or baby products
Tag the exact product, brand and colour

quote.text: the first three videos that you post are going to need to be better than the videos after that.
quote.speaker: Trevin

tactics.name: Prioritise boosted-commission products
steps: Make 20-30 videos on decently selling products to unlock the Bronze tier
Browse Creator Connections for 10-50% campaigns
Only review products with boosted rates
Check number of existing influencer videos (a beginner should avoid listings with a thousand)

tactics.name: Source products at zero cost
steps: Scan order history (own or family) for products still selling
Film items at home, Airbnbs or public places
Message brands with address to receive free products
Resell the products at a discount to recoup cost

tactics.name: Video format best practices
steps: Film horizontal for desktop
Aim for 2+ minutes
Use hook stacking: tease demo at end
Use a simple lav mic
Talk as if to a friend; use script or voiceover if shy
Add b-roll to boost retention

tactics.name: Duplicate winners
steps: When a product sells well, review similar products
Comparison videos (e.g., lav mics) perform well

warnings.warning: Amazon rejects videos with price mentions, claims, buy-now calls, license plates, labels or loud noise; failing the third approval attempt means starting again.

quote.text: if you fail on the third attempt, you can't get onsite placement.
quote.speaker: Trevin

warnings.warning: Buying then returning products is unethical and risks Amazon account closure.
Amazon can cut rates at any time.
Social profile must stay public once linked.

lessons.lesson: Piggybacking on an existing high-traffic platform removes the need to generate your own traffic.
Earnings are heavily skewed; volume of attempts matters because a small share of videos produces most income.

quote.text: It's 5% of them make 95% of them.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Asymmetric bets with near-zero cost reward consistent output.
Platform rate cuts weed out casual entrants and favour those who persist and adapt.
Boosted-commission campaigns, not standard rates, drive most income; incentives set by brands matter more than platform defaults.
A two-sided marketplace can still be early on the supply side even years in, as brands slowly learn.
Momentum beats focus: moving between ideas led the host to a better business.
Build tools for problems you personally have (the guest's origin story for Viral View).

evidence_quality.rationale: Guest gives first-hand figures for himself ($10K+/month, $12K in 30 days) but most big numbers are second-hand anecdotes about relatives and friends; no verification; survivorship bias; sells a related tool.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Guest co-founded Viral View, an Amazon influencer tool, though host says it is not a paid sponsor; host sells business plans and membership.
